decision: Framed mermaid, image preview, and PDF text indexing as one corpus-media change
why: The user asked for diagrams in answers and previews, PDF text in the index, and images or PDFs referenced from notes. PDF was an explicit unless-asked exclusion, and the user asked. A multi-hour change to the corpus contract gets a design arena before code.

decision: Grounded render, preview, chunk, and the markdown-only rule before designing
why: How traced the two hand-rolled renderers, the JSON-only preview, and the markdown glob. Why found PDF listed as out until asked, and ![[...]] specified as not a note link. The explainer's claim that PDF must become markdown first is a design guess, not a measured gate.

decision: Set the pick rubric before reading either design
why: Two bets are in flight. INDEX keeps the PDF and extracts pages into Chunk. SIDECAR writes a markdown sibling and leaves the chunker markdown-only. The rubric is one owner per invariant, honest embedded text, no renderer drift, a small public surface, an unchanged markdown path, and safe failure.

decision: Base is INDEX: PDF text becomes Chunk rows, the PDF stays the cited file
why: Sidecar writes name.pdf.md during Re-index, so search can cite text the open PDF no longer has. Judge scored INDEX 4/5/5/4/4/4 and SIDECAR 3/2/2/2/2/3.

decision: Private page extract, failed reads do not publish, shield_layout keeps fences, media route is one path

why: The lock page and the service worker must load the renderer. Corpus bytes must not.
